title: A Piece of Nepal in Every Bite
author: Pramit Bahadur Shrestha
excerpt: Discover the heart and soul behind our home-based, handmade chocolate business in Nepal and why the 'handmade' difference truly matters.
content:
🇳🇵 From Our Nepali Kitchen to Your Home


Namaste! Thank you for welcoming us into your sweet moments.


Starting a handmade chocolate business here in Nepal has always been about more than just melting cocoa and adding sugar. It’s about creating something special, something that resonates with our traditions of warmth, hospitality, and of course, our love for good food!


We know that for many of you, chocolate used to be something you only bought for special occasions, or maybe as a gift from a relative returning from abroad. But we believe the simple joy of a truly good, handmade piece of chocolate should be an everyday pleasure.


Why "Handmade" Matters to Us (and You!)


In a country where quality is often measured by the love (maya) and effort (prayas) put into something, "handmade" is our promise to you.


  • No Compromises: We source the finest cocoa we can find, and we only use real ingredients. No substitutes, no artificial flavors—just the good stuff.
  • The Power of Small Batches: Unlike the big factories, we make our chocolates in small, manageable batches. This allows us to ensure that the temperature, the texture, and the taste of every single piece is perfect before it leaves our home kitchen. Think of it like slow-cooking a delicious dal bhat—it just tastes better when it's made with patience!
  • Supporting Local: As a home-based business, every purchase you make helps a Nepali family directly. You’re not just buying chocolate; you’re supporting a dream right here in your own community.

Next time you are looking for a special treat for Tihar, a small thank you gift (dhanyabaad), or just a moment of peace after a long day in Kathmandu's traffic, remember our promise: a piece of Nepal in every bite.

title: The Art of Nepalese Gifting – Beyond the Fruit Basket
author: Pramit Bahadur Shrestha
excerpt: How handmade chocolates are becoming the modern, unique, and personal choice for traditional Nepali occasions and celebrations.
content:
🎉 Celebrating Relationships the Sweet Way


In Nepal, relationships are the heart of everything. Whether it’s celebrating a Bratabandha, a successful SLC result, or simply visiting a relative (bhetghat), we never go empty-handed. Our tradition is to offer something that shows our respect and affection.


For years, the go-to gifts have been things like new clothes, a box of sweets (mithai), or the classic fruit basket. While those are wonderful, we’ve noticed that people are looking for something more unique, personal, and universally loved.


Introducing the Modern Nepali Gift: Handmade Chocolate


Handmade chocolate is the perfect modern fusion for the Nepali tradition of gifting, and here’s why our customers love it:


  1. It’s Personal: When you gift a box of our handmade chocolates, you are giving an experience. It says, "I took the time to find something special, something made with care." Unlike mass-produced items, the imperfections in a handmade piece show its authenticity.
  2. It’s Auspicious (Shubh): Sweet foods are always considered auspicious and are essential for any new beginning or celebration. Our high-quality chocolates elevate this tradition, making the moment feel even more luxurious and memorable.
  3. The Perfect Token: Sometimes you don’t need a huge present—you just need a small, thoughtful token (koseli) for your neighbor, your child's teacher, or a colleague. Our chocolate bars and small gift boxes are perfect for these moments, showing you care without being overwhelming.

Consider swapping out the traditional laddu for a box of our truffles at your next function! We can even customize the flavors to include a hint of something Nepali, like cardamom (sukumel) or ginger (aduwa).


Need a custom gift box for your upcoming ceremony? Send us a message! We'd love to help you create a sweet memory.

title: Your Chocolate, Your Comfort: Pairing Ideas for the Nepali Climate
author: Pramit Bahadur Shrestha
excerpt: Tips on how to best enjoy our handmade chocolates throughout Nepal's diverse seasons, from winter to monsoon.
content:
🌦️ Enjoying Handmade Treats Through Every Season


Nepal's climate is famously diverse. From the bone-chilling cold of winter in the hills to the warm, humid monsoon in the Terai, our comfort foods have to adapt. And just like a cup of hotchiyais the ultimate comfort, so is the right kind of chocolate!


Here are our favorite ways to enjoy our handmade chocolates, no matter what the weather is outside:


SeasonThe Perfect Chocolate PairingWhy It Works
Winter (Poush/Magh)Hot Black Coffee or Ginger Tea (Aduwa Chiya)The rich, dark cocoa melts beautifully on your tongue and provides a satisfying, warming energy boost to combat the chill.
Monsoon (Asar/Shrawan)Spicy Masala Tea (Masala Chiya) or a Strong EspressoThe fragrant spices in the tea cut through the richness of the chocolate, and the slightly dreary weather makes a cozy, indulgent treat feel just right.
Spring/Autumn (Basanta/Sharad)A cool glass of Lassi or Plain WaterThese milder seasons call for a simpler pairing. A sip of plain water before a piece of chocolate helps you appreciate the pure, complex flavor notes of the cocoa bean.

A Note on Storage (Especially During the Heat)


Since our chocolates are made without industrial preservatives, they are sensitive to temperature!


  • During the hot months, please store your chocolates in an airtight container in the refrigerator.Wait about5-10 minutesafter taking them out before eating. This allows the flavor to truly bloom without the chocolate being too hard.
  • Avoid leaving them in a car or near a window—they'll melt faster than you can say 'Mero chocolate kahan gayo?!' (Where did my chocolate go?!).

We hope these tips help you savor every single piece!
